quizName: Input, Processing, Memory, Storage, and Output
description: Review input, processing, working memory, storage, and output. Practice following information through a computer and recognizing devices that can do more than one job.

questionVariants: What does the input job do in a computing system?
How does information move during input?
What happens when a computer carries out its input job?
What is meant by input when describing a computer's work?
What is the purpose of the input job?
answerVariants: Data or commands enter the system for it to use.
Information or directions come into the machine from a source.
The system takes in information or commands.
Data or instructions arrive from a source outside the task being done.
The machine receives information or directions to use in its work.

questionVariants: How can a sensor gather facts about the room around it?
What job does a sensor do before its results can be used by a computer?
How does a sensor collect data without someone typing it in?
What does a sensor do when checking the air in a classroom?
How does a sensor help a machine learn about its surroundings?
answerVariants: It measures a physical condition, such as temperature, and supplies the reading.
It takes a measurement of a real-world condition and passes on the reading.
It checks a physical condition and provides a measurement for the system to use.
It measures something in the physical world and sends that reading to the system.
It collects a measurement, such as how warm the air is, and passes it along.

questionVariants: What is processing in a computing system?
What does the processing job involve?
How would you explain processing to a classmate?
What happens during the processing part of a computer task?
What does it mean when a computer is processing data?
answerVariants: Following instructions to do work on information.
Carrying out steps that act on information.
Using directions or rules to work on information.
Following a set of instructions to handle information.
Doing work on information by carrying out given steps.

concepts.conceptName: The CPU Is a Main Processing Part
questionVariants: What main computer part is often shortened to CPU?
What does the name CPU stand for?
Write out the full name behind the letters CPU.
What is the full name of the main chip known as the CPU?
Which full name belongs to the computer part called the CPU?
answerVariants: Central processing unit, a main part that follows instructions.
The central processing unit, a main part that does work on data.
A central processing unit, a main part used to carry out instructions.
Central processing unit, the main part that carries out instructions.
The central processing unit, a main part for carrying out instructions.

questionVariants: How can other chips help the CPU with certain tasks?
Why might a computer have chips besides its main CPU to help do work?
How can a computer use extra chips to help with a particular type of work?
What kind of help can other chips provide alongside a computer's CPU?
How can a machine share some work with chips other than its main CPU?
answerVariants: Special processors can be built for one particular kind of job.
Special-purpose processors handle a certain kind of job instead of many kinds.
Processors designed for a specific job can handle that part of the task.
Special processors focus on a particular kind of job.
Processors made for specific jobs can take on those duties.

concepts.conceptName: RAM Holds Work in Use Now
questionVariants: What job does RAM do while a computer is running?
Why does a computer use RAM during a task?
What does RAM hold ready for a computer to use?
How does RAM help with the work a computer is doing now?
What is the purpose of RAM during a program's work?
answerVariants: Fast working memory holds the data and instructions in use right now.
A fast workspace keeps information and directions ready for the current task.
Fast temporary memory holds the information and instructions being used at the moment.
A fast workspace holds the data and directions needed for the current task.
Fast working memory keeps current information and instructions close at hand.

concepts.conceptName: Persistent Storage Keeps Files for Later
questionVariants: What does persistent storage do that a temporary workspace cannot?
Why is persistent storage useful when you shut a computer down?
What job does persistent storage have after power is switched off?
How does persistent storage help you use your work another day?
Why does a computer need persistent storage as well as a temporary workspace?
answerVariants: It keeps saved files and programs available even without power.
It holds saved work and programs for later use, including after shutdown.
Saved information and programs stay there even when the machine is off.
It keeps saved work and programs for later without needing the machine to stay on.
It preserves saved information and programs through a shutdown for use later.

questionVariants: What is the output job in a computing system?
What does output give after a computer does its work?
How would you explain output to a classmate?
What can a computer produce as output?
What is meant by output in a computer task?
answerVariants: Information or an action produced as a result.
A result that may be information or physical movement.
Information or a physical effect that the system produces.
A result, such as a message, sound, or movement.
Information or an action that comes from the system's work.

questionVariants: How does haptic feedback reach a person using a device?
What can you feel when a device gives haptic feedback?
What does haptic feedback mean for someone using a device?
How is haptic feedback different from a picture or sound?
What kind of signal does haptic feedback provide?
answerVariants: A vibration from a small motor gives a signal through touch.
A small motor makes a vibration that you feel through touch.
A motor makes the device buzz, giving a signal you can feel.
A felt vibration, made by a small motor, carries the signal.
A small motor produces a touch signal by making the device vibrate.

questionVariants: How does a touchscreen do both an input job and an output job?
Why can a touchscreen count as both input and output?
What two things does a touchscreen do that give it an input role and an output role?
What two jobs allow a touchscreen to work in both directions?
What makes a touchscreen more than an output-only device?
answerVariants: Detects where you press and displays pictures and text.
Senses a finger's presses and presents words and pictures.
Tracks where a finger presses and displays information for you to see.
Detects finger presses and presents visible information.
Senses where you press while presenting pictures and words.

concepts.conceptName: A Network Interface Sends and Receives
questionVariants: How does a network interface do both an input job and an output job?
Why can a network interface work in both directions?
What two jobs give a network interface its input and output roles?
How can a network interface act as more than an input-only part?
What makes a network interface both an input part and an output part?
answerVariants: Receives messages from other machines and sends messages back to them.
Accepts incoming messages from other machines and delivers outgoing ones to them.
Takes in messages from other machines and passes messages out to them.
Sends messages to other machines as well as receiving messages from them.
Brings in messages from other machines and delivers messages back out to them.

concepts.conceptName: Writing and Reading Move Stored Data
questionVariants: How does data move on a drive when you save a file and later open it?
Compare the directions data travels when you save a file and open it later.
What opposite actions happen inside a drive when a file is saved and then opened?
Describe the two directions data moves on a drive during a file save and a later file open.
How does a drive handle data differently when you save your work and when you open it again?
answerVariants: Writing puts data into the device; reading brings saved data back out.
Writing sends data into the device, while reading returns what was kept there.
Writing means putting data in; reading means getting kept data back out.
During writing, data goes into the device; during reading, kept data comes back out.
Writing places data inside the device, and reading gets that saved data back.

concepts.conceptName: Role Names Describe the Current Job
questionVariants: What decides whether a device acts as input or output during an activity?
Why can one device be called input in one activity and output in another?
How should you decide which information role a device has?
What should you examine before calling a device input, processing, storage, or output?
Why should you avoid giving a device one permanent information-role label?
answerVariants: Look at what it is doing with data at that moment; the job can change with the task.
Its job depends on how data moves in the task being done, rather than on one fixed category.
Examine its current job with data, since that job can change in another task.
Follow the data and the job being done now, instead of assuming the same job always applies.
The current job with data matters; another task may give the same part a different job.
